what_was_done: One local-delivery rule, as proposed except for the dirty case: detached merge in the integration worktree, then update-ref or a fast-forward of the checkout that holds the branch. A refused fast-forward returns `checkout_dirty` (blocked, no decision the first time, rerun after cleaning) instead of awaiting_merge, because a merge decision cannot clean a checkout and would cost the person a second command. `vsdd release` moves its branch the same way; the delivery tests cover the checkout clean, overlapping, non-overlapping, absent and moved.

Rules never test the payload cwd alone: `where`, the call's effective directory (the target's directory, or the directory a cd, git -C or vsdd -C names), defines the caller's worktree. The lock is refreshed only by calls that belong to the run (a vsdd call with its --run, a StructuredOutput with its step.run, a call in its worktrees, a subagent call in the holder's session). If updatedInput is not honoured the marker is found by a hash of the call's arguments, oldest unread first, so item 29 no longer gates anything but the offered cut.

what_was_done: Adopted `checkout_dirty` as the state for a checkout the merge would overwrite, but not merging in the person's checkout: the merge commit is always made in the tool's detached integration worktree, so a conflict never lands in the person's files, and their checkout only ever receives a fast-forward that git refuses atomically. The invariant wording is amended; init and doctor need no change because the checkout on the integration branch is the normal, supported case.

merge-guard now blocks, for every caller, commands that move, replace or delete the integration or release branch without a checkout (update-ref, symbolic-ref, branch -f/-m/-M/-c/-C/-d/-D, switch -C, checkout -B, fetch, pull and push refspecs). Those commands sit in the new git-other family, which no builder holds. The proposed integration_moved refusal was not taken: a person in local mode, and other people's merges in pr mode, move the branch legitimately; local delivery re-merges from the new head instead.

`method` is in the step identity and so in every step record; a pass counts only when its method belongs to a reviewer-tier agent in the methods table and the stored agent type is that owner. A conformance fixture has a builder echo a reviewer's method.

Each rule module is imported inside its own rule's try, so an import error is that rule's rule.error and the quarantine condition can be met. The rule_error block's fix line names the restart with VSDD_FACTORY_HOOKS_QUARANTINE=<rule>, and the briefing's state-problems line and vsdd status list rules with repeated rule.error. Copying block codes into a blocked packet was not taken: the briefing line already reaches the person.

Resolved by the local-delivery rule in story-deliver, not by the proposal. Keeping the integration branch out of the person's checkout was rejected: it makes a person leave their own branch in every project with no remote and merge by hand to see delivered work, which is high touch. The checkout on the integration branch is the supported case, so init, doctor and the sample need no special handling, and the slice fixture keeps the checkout on that branch.

The step identity carries method, loop and pass; story.js names review, fix and arbitrate steps with the loop and pass (review-<lens>-l<n>-p<k>), so a scoped re-review writes new records. verdicts.md now defines what the tool rebuilds: passes, items to account for, disputes, rulings, waivers, the cap and `used`, the order of loops across runs, and when a verdict covers a head; the conformance table gains a case per input.

what_was_done: The design now says what was built: the Playwright entry carries no option, because the pinned server refuses file: addresses by default; L-MCP rejects --allow-unrestricted-file-access; probe 33 confirms the default on the running server.

The discriminator the launcher uses is now in the design: on uv exit 2 only, it runs `uv python find --no-python-downloads '>=3.11'` with a cache of its own; an interpreter found means uv is at fault (uv_unusable), none means the Python floor (py_floor).

The design now says neither entry execs uv, and gives the cli entry's exit mapping: 0 and 1 pass through silently, 2 runs the interpreter probe and adds the uv fix only when no Python is found, any other code is reported. The code is wrong on one point: in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/launch.sh the cli branch's `*)` case prints `the vsdd tool could not run (exit 1)` for vsdd's own negative answer; it needs a `1) exit 1 ;;` case before it, with a test.

The contents of next/.gitignore are specified as built: /.mcp.json with the negation !/plugins/vsdd-factory/.mcp.json, .claude/worktrees/, /.worktrees/, settings.local.json, caches and node_modules, with the reason the negation is needed during the rewrite.

The design now says the launcher writes runner.launch_failed and runner.disabled itself, with v, ts in whole seconds, type, severity, session_id null, code and mode, into the same directory and honouring VSDD_EVENTS_DIR; the event schema admits a null session_id and both timestamp forms. The launcher matches. events.py does not: EVENT_SCHEMA in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/events.py requires a non-empty string session_id and a millisecond timestamp, so the schema it prints rejects the launcher's lines; it must accept null and whole seconds for reading while the Python writer keeps writing its own strict form.

The design now states that every shape (step result, step data, tool outputs, records) is a schema file under <plugin>/schemas/ delivered by C1, and that every S_* literal in the prelude is generated from its file. The code does not do this yet: next/workflow-lib/prelude.js writes S_REVIEW, S_FIXES, S_RULINGS, S_HOLDOUT, S_SURVEY, S_CLOSE, S_DELIVERY and S_WAVE_GATE by hand, and next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/ has no survey, checkpoint-result, delivery-data, story-unit, wave-gate-data or implement-data file. C1 must add those files and tools/build.py must generate the literals and fail --check on a hand-written one.

The reader's semantics are pinned as built: refused, not misread. On every input it accepts it equals PyYAML's YAML 1.1 safe_load, and every plain scalar YAML 1.1 would retype is refused with the line number. The differential test is extended to artifact frontmatter in the fixture overlays and hook case files and to a corpus of inputs that must be refused; the first of these is added to the built test when those fixtures exist.

enc() is specified as built: encodeURIComponent plus the five characters it leaves raw (! ' ( ) *). Universal test 11 passes a request with both quotes, a semicolon, parentheses, an asterisk and an exclamation mark and requires that none appears raw.

The holdout finding's shape is settled as built: location is {"path": ""}, owner is product-owner, and holdoutFindings(unit, scores, opts) takes its thresholds from the survey's config.holdout (not limits) and its spec_ref and seed from a new `holdout` field (seed, contracts by scenario) in the output of gate wave and gate release, because only the tool can read a scenario.

The harness table now lists what the builder implemented: log(), budget.total and remaining(), pipeline(items, ...stages) with stages receiving (prev, item, index), workflow() returning the child's value and throwing when it threw, agents counted and workflow() calls not; and the schema rule is corrected to `required` optional and a subset of properties.

Universal tests 4, 5 and 7 now say that every stub returns as `step` the identity its prompt gave it and that the survey stub passes with the units the test supplies, which is what the built tests do; test 4 also asserts that the loops ran.

The checkpoint output is typed: ok and error, plus status, progress, decisions and next exactly as the workflow-result schema types them, all required. The built S_CLOSE has the same types; its required list (ok, status, next) grows to all six when the literals are generated from the schema files.
